docs.title: Flo, the Kubeflow docs assistant
docs.text:
Flo answers questions about Kubeflow from the official documentation, GitHub issues and source code, and shows the sources it used. It is an agentic RAG system that runs entirely on Kubernetes: the agent decides which search tool to call, the tools search a vector database, and a self-hosted model writes the answer.

The project is kubeflow/docs-agent. It started as a Google Summer of Code 2026 project and is becoming a subproject of the Kubeflow Agents working group.

  • Architecture

    How a question becomes an answer: agents, MCP tools, hybrid retrieval, models, and the public gateway.

    Architecture

  • Contributing

    How to make a change, how it reaches users, and how to see what it did to answer quality.

    Contributing

  • Evaluation and feedback

    The eval that runs on every merge, and how thumbs-down from real users turn into issues.

    Evaluation

  • Operations

    Environments and promotion, Argo CD, tracing and data retention, ingestion.

    Operations

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text: Part What it is Agents kagent Agent resources: a docs agent (thinking off and on) and a debug agent Tools An MCP server with search_kubeflow_docs, search_github_issues, search_kubeflow_code Retrieval Milvus, hybrid dense + BM25 search chosen per query by an intent router Models Gemma 4 E4B answers; Qwen2.5-7B judges evaluations. Both served by KServe/vLLM, one GPU each Edge Istio gateway with TLS, rate limits, CORS allow-list and anonymous session tokens Delivery Argo CD; staging deploys every commit on main, production is promoted to a tested commit every week or two Quality A 58-question end-to-end eval on every merge; user feedback with nightly triage Privacy Anonymous sessions; conversations and feedback kept 4 weeks (what we collect) Tracing OpenTelemetry and Langfuse, with live and evaluation traces kept apart

docs.title: The path of one question
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant U as User (docs site widget)
    participant G as Istio gateway
    participant A as kagent docs agent
    participant L as Gemma (KServe)
    participant M as MCP server
    participant V as Milvus
    U->>G: POST /api/session (anonymous token)
    U->>G: A2A message/stream + token
    G->>A: route (rate-limited, token checked)
    A->>L: question + tool schemas
    L-->>A: call search_kubeflow_docs(query)
    A->>M: tool call
    M->>V: intent router: BM25, hybrid or dense
    V-->>M: chunks
    M-->>A: evidence + structured citations
    A->>L: evidence
    L-->>A: grounded answer
    A-->>U: streamed answer, Sources panel, 👍 / 👎

docs.title: What we collect
docs.text:
Flo is an open-source assistant run by the Kubeflow community. To find and fix wrong answers, it records conversations. The chat widget says so under the input box:

Conversations and feedback are recorded to improve answer quality, so please don't share personal information.

docs.title: What is recorded
docs.text: Data Why Your questions and Flo's answers, with the searches and sources behind each answer To see where retrieval or the answer went wrong 👍 / 👎 votes and the optional comment To find bad answers and route them to the right maintainers Timing and token counts To keep the service fast and within its GPU budget

docs.title: What is not recorded
docs.text:
• No accounts. The widget gets an anonymous session token that expires after 30 minutes. It identifies a chat, not a person.
  • No names or emails. Nothing ties a conversation to who asked it, unless you type it into the chat yourself.

docs.title: Who can see it and for how long
docs.text:
• Conversations and feedback are visible only to the project's maintainers and mentors, in a self-hosted Langfuse instance in the project's own cluster.
  • They are deleted after 4 weeks by a weekly job. Evaluation runs, which use the project's own test questions and no user data, are deleted after 2 weeks.

Details for operators: Observability.

docs.title: Triage labels
docs.text:
Canonical label strings for docs-agent issue triage. Create them with ./scripts/sync-github-labels.sh <owner/repo> before the first analyzer run. GitHub Agentic Workflows will not apply a label that is missing from the repo or from the workflow safe-outputs.add-labels.allowed list.

Issue titles must be <type>(<area>): <summary>. Templates seed that format. The analyzer treats the parsed type and area as trusted metadata; the issue body is untrusted.

docs.title: Kind (exactly one)
docs.text: Title type Label Meaning bug kind/bug Something is broken in current behavior feat kind/feature New capability chore kind/chore Cleanup, refactor, dependency, ops docs kind/docs Documentation only test kind/chore + area/tests Test-only change ci kind/chore + area/ci GitHub Actions / CD security kind/security Auth, injection, XSS, secrets, mesh

docs.title: Area (exactly one)
docs.text:
Token in the title maps to one area/* label. Aliases live in area-map.json.

Title area Label Read first mcp area/mcp docs-agent-mcp/mcp-server/server.py pipelines area/pipelines docs-agent-mcp/pipelines/ frontend area/frontend frontend/docs_scripts/chatbot.js kagent area/kagent docs-agent-mcp/manifests/kagent/setup.yaml gateway area/gateway docs-agent-mcp/charts/gateway-guardrails/ terraform area/terraform docs-agent-mcp/terraform/ embeddings area/embeddings docs-agent-mcp/mcp-server/embeddings_client.py ci area/ci .github/workflows/ tests area/tests tests/ docs area/docs README.md, docs/agents/ infra area/infra Milvus, KServe, Istio, namespaces

Use area/mcp for FastMCP tools, retrieval bugs, MCP Deployment, and the /mcp handshake. Do not invent area/mcp-server; that alias resolves to area/mcp.

docs.title: Status and routing (optional)
docs.text: Label When needs-triage Default from templates; remove once the analyzer (or a maintainer) finishes needs-info Missing repro, expected/actual, logs, or environment good first issue Scoped, documented, no cluster required help wanted Maintainers want external help maintainer-only Agentic RAG core — design discussion first gsoc-2026 Tracked in gsoc2026_agentic_rag.md duplicate Same defect as another issue; cite #N in the comment

docs.title: Priority (at most one)
docs.text:
Label When priority/p0 Security incident, data loss, or public-bot outage priority/p1 Major regression or blocker with no workaround priority/p2 Normal actionable work

Prefer leaving priority unset over guessing.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Flo is four loosely coupled layers plus the platform around them. Each layer can be changed, deployed and evaluated on its own.

flowchart LR
  subgraph edge["Edge (gateway-guardrails)"]
    W[Docs-site widget] --> GW[Istio gateway<br/>TLS · rate limits · CORS · session JWT]
    GW --> FB[feedback service]
  end
  subgraph agent["Agents (docs-agent chart, namespace docs-agent)"]
    GW --> KA[kagent agents<br/>docs · docs-think · debug]
    KA --> MCP[MCP server<br/>3 search tools]
  end
  subgraph infra["Models and data (namespace ml-infra)"]
    KA --> LLM[Gemma 4 E4B<br/>llm-runtime · GPU 1]
    MCP --> EMB[TEI embeddings]
    MCP --> MV[(Milvus<br/>docs · issues · code)]
    JUDGE[Qwen2.5-7B judge<br/>llm-judge · GPU 2]
  end
  subgraph ingest["Ingestion (Kubeflow Pipelines)"]
    SRC[kubeflow/website<br/>GitHub issues · code] --> KFP[KFP pipelines] --> MV
  end
  subgraph obs["Observability"]
    KA -. spans .-> OT[OTel collector] --> LF[Langfuse]
    MCP -. spans .-> LF
    FB --> LF
  end

docs.title: Layers
docs.text: Layer What it does Code Edge Public entry point. Only the agent stream, session and feedback paths are routed; everything else returns 404. docs-agent-mcp/charts/gateway-guardrails/ Agents kagent Agent, ModelConfig and RemoteMCPServer resources. The agent decides when to search and which tool to use. docs-agent-mcp/charts/docs-agent/ Tools FastMCP server. An intent router picks BM25, hybrid or dense search per query; results carry structured citations. docs-agent-mcp/mcp-server/ Models One model per GPU through KServe and vLLM. The answer model and the judge model are separate releases of the same chart. docs-agent-mcp/charts/llm-runtime/ Data Milvus collections kubeflow_docs, issues_rag, code_rag; 768-d MPNet embeddings from a TEI service. docs-agent-mcp/pipelines/ Widget Chat UI on the docs site: streaming, Sources panel, persona and thinking toggles, answer feedback. frontend/

docs.title: gateway-guardrails
docs.text: Helm chart for the public gateway of the Kubeflow docs-agent chatbot. This chart is the single source of truth for the Istio edge config — it replaces the raw kubectl_manifest heredocs that previously lived in terraform/istio_policies.tf and terraform/kagent_ingress.tf, and the standalone YAML under manifests/istio*.

docs.title: What it manages
docs.text: Layer Resources Toggle TLS ClusterIssuer (Let's Encrypt) + Certificate gateway.tls.acme.enabled Routing Gateway + VirtualService: only /api/session, the JWKS and the A2A stream are public (CORS lockdown, 300s stream timeout) gateway.enabled Rate limit L1 a2a-global-ratelimit EnvoyFilter — 60 req/min token bucket on the :443 listener rateLimit.global.enabled Rate limit L2 Envoy ratelimit service + Redis + EnvoyFilter — 10 req/min per client IP rateLimit.perIP.enabled (off: needs real client IPs, see below) Mesh policies AuthorizationPolicies for the RAG stack (Milvus, MCP, embeddings, plus one per meshPolicies.llmInferenceServiceNames entry) meshPolicies.enabled

docs.title: Why
docs.text: The chatbot is backed by a single GPU-served LLM. Without limits, one script can exhaust GPU capacity (cost + DoS), and wide-open CORS let any origin embed it. These guardrails cap request volume and lock down who may call the endpoint — all at the Istio ingress, with no application changes.

docs.title: Install / upgrade
docs.text:
The ACME HTTP-01 solver needs the istio IngressClass. Apply it once per cluster: kubectl apply -f ../../manifests/istio-tls/ingress-class.yaml. domain and gateway.tls.acme.email have no defaults. Terraform sets them from kagent_domain_name and kagent_acme_email; for a manual upgrade, pass them:

helm upgrade --install gateway-guardrails . -n docs-agent \
  --set domain=agent.your-domain.example \
  --set gateway.tls.acme.email=you@your-domain.example

To keep the contact email out of values (for example with Argo CD reading values from Git), create the ClusterIssuer once as a cluster admin and set gateway.tls.acme.createIssuer=false; the Certificate then references the existing clusterIssuerName. On a release that already created the issuer, first run kubectl annotate clusterissuer letsencrypt-prod helm.sh/resource-policy=keep so the upgrade does not delete it.

Session tokens are enforced (sessionAuth.enforce: true) on /a2a/* and /api/a2a/*: a request without a valid token from POST /api/session gets a 403.

Tuning examples:

--set rateLimit.global.requestsPerMinute=120
--set routing.cors.allowOrigins[0].exact=https://your-widget.example.app

docs.title: Per-IP rate limit prerequisite
docs.text: rateLimit.perIP ships disabled: the ingress Service runs externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster, so client IPs are SNAT'd to node IPs and a per-IP descriptor would act as one shared bucket — effectively a second, tighter global limit rather than per-client fairness. Before enabling, either set externalTrafficPolicy: Local on the ingress Service (and verify the LB health checks) or trust XFF via meshConfig.numTrustedProxies.

docs.title: Verifying
docs.text:
# Exposure: kagent's admin API (no auth) must not be reachable; expect 404 for all
for p in / /api/agents /api/sessions /api/toolservers '/a2a/..%2fapi/sessions'; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} $p\n" --path-as-is "https://$DOMAIN$p"; done

# Session auth: no token -> 403
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST https://$DOMAIN/a2a/docs-agent/kubeflow-docs-agent \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'

# CORS: a foreign origin must get no access-control-allow-origin header
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST https://$DOMAIN/api/session | jq -r .access_token)
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - https://$DOMAIN/api/a2a/docs-agent/kubeflow-docs-agent/.well-known/agent.json \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Origin: https://evil.example" | grep -i access-control-allow-origin

# Rate limit: expect 429s past the per-minute cap (403 for the rest: no token)
seq 1 100 | xargs -P 25 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \
  -X POST https://$DOMAIN/api/a2a/docs-agent/kubeflow-docs-agent \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"t","method":"x"}' | sort | uniq -c

# CORS: the allowed origin gets an allow-origin header; others do not
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - -X OPTIONS https://$DOMAIN/api/a2a/docs-agent/kubeflow-docs-agent \
  -H "Origin: https://your-widget.example.app" -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: POST" \
  | grep -i access-control-allow-origin

docs.title: Note on the shared ingress gateway
docs.text:
knative-ingress-gateway and knative-local-gateway also select istio: ingressgateway (the agent → LLM path rides knative-local on the same pod). The rate-limit EnvoyFilter is therefore scoped to the :443 listener so it never applies to the knative / internal LLM listeners.

This page is docs-agent-mcp/charts/gateway-guardrails/README.md from the repository, included as is so there is one copy. Edit it there.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Two models run in the cluster, each on its own GPU, both deployed with the llm-runtime Helm chart (KServe with vLLM).

Release Model Served as Used by llm-runtime Gemma 4 E4B flo-llm The agents, to answer questions llm-judge Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (AWQ) flo-judge The eval Job, feedback triage, Langfuse evaluators

docs.title: The answer model
docs.text:
Gemma 4 E4B was chosen by evaluation against Qwen2.5-7B:

Qwen2.5-7B Gemma 4 E4B Retrieval hit@5 (22 questions) 22/22 22/22 Faithfulness 0.71 0.69 Correctness 0.75 0.75 Tool-use cases passed (of 291) 168 270 Mean latency 17.3 s 4.4 s

Answer quality is level, tool use is much better, and answers are about four times faster. Two ModelConfigs point at it: flo-llm (thinking off) and flo-llm-think (thinking on, used by the docs agent's thinking variant).

docs.title: The judge
docs.text: A model that grades its own answers rates them generously. The judge is a different model family, so evaluations do not grade Gemma with Gemma, and judging never takes GPU time from users. Its scores are used to compare commits on the same questions.

docs.title: Switching models
docs.text:
The agents always call the served name flo-llm, so switching the answer model is one value, model, in the llm-runtime release. Profiles for both models are in the chart's catalog. A switch restarts the GPU pod and reloads weights, so the llm-runtime and llm-judge applications are synced by hand in Argo CD.

Chart values and commands: docs-agent-mcp/charts/llm-runtime/README.md.

docs.title: Retrieval
docs.text:
The MCP server turns a search query into evidence the model can quote and citations the widget can show. It searches three Milvus collections, one per source.

Tool Collection Use it for search_kubeflow_docs kubeflow_docs How-to and conceptual content, versions and releases search_github_issues issues_rag Error messages, symptoms, "has anyone hit this" search_kubeflow_code code_rag Defaults, CRD fields, manifests, controller behaviour

The agent chooses the tool. Each tool's description says what it is for and what it is not for, so the routing decision is explicit.

docs.title: Hybrid search and the intent router
docs.text:
Embeddings are good at meaning and weak at exact tokens such as version numbers, config keys and error strings. The docs collection therefore stores both a dense vector and a native BM25 sparse vector, and a rule-based intent router picks the search mode for each query. No model is involved.

Intent Example Mode After search comparison "compare 1.9 and 1.10" hybrid, deeper candidate pool – release_date "when was 1.10 released" BM25 prefer chunks for that version temporal "what is the latest release" BM25 on release notes sort by release date exact a version, a dotted config key, an error string BM25 – conceptual "how", "why", "explain" hybrid – general anything else hybrid –

Hybrid search fuses the dense and BM25 results with reciprocal rank fusion (hybridRanker: rrf; a weighted ranker is available). A collection without the BM25 field falls back to dense search. The chosen intent, mode and reason are returned with every result and recorded in the trace.

docs.title: Collection schema (docs)
docs.text:
Field Purpose content_text Chunk text; also the BM25 input vector 768-dimension dense embedding (MPNet, from the TEI service) sparse_vector BM25 output, computed by Milvus document_id, chunk_index Stable document key and chunk position title, section_path Page title and heading breadcrumb citation_url, file_path Public URL and source path doc_type, version, release_date Release notes vs docs, the Kubeflow version, and its release date

Indexes: a flat cosine index on vector and an inverted BM25 index on sparse_vector.

docs.title: The citation contract
docs.text:
Part Responsibility MCP evidence Chunk text with URLs removed, labelled [c1], [c2], … MCP structured result citations: a list of {id, url, score, section, version, …} Agent Answers from the evidence and never prints URLs or source lists Widget Renders the Sources panel from the structured citations

Because the model never sees a URL, it cannot invent one. Links always come from the index.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• docs-agent-mcp/mcp-server/server.py: the three MCP tools
  • docs-agent-mcp/mcp-server/intent_router.py: intent rules
  • docs-agent-mcp/mcp-server/milvus_search.py: dense, BM25 and hybrid search
  • docs-agent-mcp/mcp-server/citations.py: evidence and citation formatting

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Thanks for helping. docs-agent follows the Kubeflow contributor guide: sign your commits for the DCO (git commit -s), open a pull request against main, and a reviewer approves it with /lgtm and /approve.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text: You want to Look at Improve answers Prompts in docs-agent-mcp/charts/docs-agent/files/, retrieval in docs-agent-mcp/mcp-server/ Improve the chat widget frontend/docs_scripts/chatbot.js, frontend/docs_styles/chatbot.css Add or fix ingestion docs-agent-mcp/pipelines/ Deployment and charts docs-agent-mcp/charts/, deploy/ Evals tests/eval/ A first issue Issues labelled good first issue, and issues filed from the nightly triage report

docs.title: Before you open a PR
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements-test.txt ruff==0.15.9
ruff check .
ruff format --check docs-agent-mcp/mcp-server tests
pytest -q
helm lint docs-agent-mcp/charts/docs-agent

CI runs the same checks, compiles the Kubeflow pipelines in their own environment, and renders every chart.

docs.title: Opening issues
docs.text:
Use a title of the form <type>(<area>): <summary>, so the issue triage workflow can attach source context and labels.

  • Types: bug, feat, chore, docs, test, ci, security
  • Areas: mcp, pipelines, frontend, kagent, gateway, terraform, embeddings, ci, tests, docs, infra

Example: bug(mcp): search_kubeflow_docs returns Search failed on empty collection.

docs.title: After your PR merges
docs.text: Your change goes to staging automatically and is evaluated, and reaches production with the next promotion (every week or two). See How a change reaches users for the full path and for how to find your eval run.

docs.title: This documentation
docs.text:
The site is built with MkDocs Material from docs/ and mkdocs.yml, and published to GitHub Pages when a change to docs/ merges. Two pages include the READMEs that sit next to the code (Gateway and security, Ingestion pipelines), so edit those READMEs and the site picks them up.

pip install "mkdocs-material==9.6.*"
mkdocs serve          # http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build --strict # what CI runs on every docs PR

docs.title: How a change reaches users
docs.text:
An example: @alice improves how the docs agent searches Katib pages.

flowchart TB
  A["1 · PR to main<br/>CI: lint, tests, pipeline compile, chart render"] --> B["2 · Review<br/>/lgtm /approve, Prow merges"]
  B --> C["3 · Build<br/>CI pushes both images tagged with the commit"]
  C --> D["4 · Staging<br/>Argo CD syncs docs-agent-staging to that commit"]
  D --> E["5 · Eval<br/>58 questions, judged by Qwen<br/>Experiment '<commit> pr-<n> @alice'"]
  E --> F["6 · Promotion<br/>every week or two, a promotion PR<br/>moves production to a tested commit"]
  F --> G["7 · Users<br/>traces, 👍/👎, nightly triage"]
  G -->|issues| A
Step What happens Where to look 1. PR CI checks the code; no cluster access The PR's checks 2. Review A reviewer approves; Prow merges The PR 3. Build On main, CI builds and pushes ghcr.io/kubeflow/mcp-kubeflow-docs:<short sha> and ghcr.io/kubeflow/kubeflow-session-issuer:<short sha> Actions run summary 4. Staging Argo CD syncs docs-agent-staging to the new commit and its image Argo CD, app docs-agent-staging 5. Eval The PostSync Job grades 58 questions; a failed gate fails the sync Langfuse evaluation project → Experiments, run named <short sha> … 6. Promotion A maintainer runs deploy/promote.sh; the PR lists every commit since the last release, yours included, with the eval scores. Merging it deploys production. The promotion PR, Argo CD app docs-agent 7. Users Answers are traced; feedback is triaged each night Langfuse live project (maintainers)

Your change is in production after the first promotion that includes your commit. Promotions happen every week or two; ask in the PR if a fix needs to go out sooner.

docs.title: What to check on your eval run
docs.text:
• Routing stayed at or near 1.0. A drop means the agent stopped calling the right tool for some questions; open the failing items to see which.
  • Grounded did not fall compared with the previous run on main. Items rated partial or no have the judge's reason in the score comment.
  • Latency did not jump.

The judge is a small model, so compare runs rather than reading one score in isolation.

docs.title: Changes that need extra care
docs.text:
• Models: a change to llm-runtime restarts the GPU pod; it is synced by hand, after an eval on the second GPU or with tests/eval/slm_tool_eval.py.
  • Gateway: a change to gateway-guardrails affects public routing and security. It reaches production with the next promotion, so call it out in your PR description for the person promoting.
  • Secrets: never in a PR. Ask a maintainer.

docs.title: Evaluation and feedback
docs.text:
Two loops tell us whether Flo is getting better:

Loop When Question it answers Results Eval on every merge After each merge, when staging syncs the new commit Did this change break routing or grounding? Langfuse evaluation project, Experiments Feedback and triage Every user 👍/👎, triaged nightly Where do real answers fail, and who should fix it? Langfuse live project, scores and a report

All judging uses flo-judge (Qwen2.5-7B), a different model from the one that answers, on its own GPU. See Models.

docs.title: Eval on every merge
docs.text:
Staging takes its image from the commit it syncs, so every merge to main changes staging and triggers a sync. After each sync, a Job sends 58 real questions through the whole deployed stack (agent, MCP tools, Milvus, model), grades the answers, and records the run in Langfuse. If a gate fails, the Job fails and Argo CD marks the sync as failed.

Promotion to production does not run another eval: production gets the same commit that staging already evaluated, and the promotion PR records that commit's scores.

docs.title: What it checks
docs.text:
The cases are the single-turn questions in tests/eval/flo_eval_dataset.json: docs routing, issues routing, debug routing, query fidelity, and small talk that should not trigger a search.

Score Meaning Gate routing The agent called an expected tool, or no tool for small talk ≥ 0.85 query_fidelity The search query kept the key terms of the question reported grounded The judge finds every claim supported by what the tools returned (yes / partial / no) share of yes ≥ 0.65 answers The answer addresses the question reported errors Any failed request 0

Latest baseline (staging, October 2026): routing 1.00, query fidelity 1.00, grounded 0.73, answers 0.78, median latency 2.6 s.

docs.title: Finding your run
docs.text:
1. Log in to Langfuse with the community account and open the evaluation project.
  2. Go to Experiments (also under Datasets → flo-e2e).
  3. Runs are named <short sha> pr-<number> @<author> <time>. Find yours by commit, PR number or GitHub username.
  4. Open the run to see each question, the agent's answer, the expected tools and the four scores. Select two runs to compare them side by side.
  5. Each item links to the agent's full trace (agent_trace_id in its metadata).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Chart: docs-agent-mcp/charts/docs-agent/templates/eval-job.yaml, enabled with eval.enabled (on in staging only). It is an Argo CD PostSync hook.
  • The Job downloads tests/eval/staging_eval.py and the dataset at the synced commit, so the eval always matches the deployed code. Standard library only.
  • It talks to the agents through the kagent controller's A2A API, and uses a unique A2A contextId per question, which becomes the Langfuse session id.
  • Results are written as Langfuse v4 Experiments (spans with langfuse.experiment.* attributes) plus scores on each agent trace.

docs.title: Running it yourself
docs.text:
# against staging, from a laptop with port-forwards to the kagent controller and the judge
AGENT_BASE=http://localhost:8083 \
JUDGE_URL=http://localhost:8091/v1/chat/completions \
LIMIT=5 python tests/eval/staging_eval.py

Without Langfuse keys the results are printed but not recorded. LIMIT runs only the first N cases; the chart value eval.limit does the same for a smoke run.

Runs are kept in Langfuse for two weeks (see Data retention); the dataset itself is kept.

docs.title: Feedback and triage
docs.text:
Real users tell us where Flo fails. Every answer in the chat widget has a Helpful? 👍 👎 bar; a thumbs-down can carry a comment. Each night a triage job works out why those answers failed and who owns the fix.

Status

The feedback bar, the feedback service and the triage CronJob arrive with kubeflow/docs-agent#268.

What users are told about this data, and how long it is kept, is on What we collect.

flowchart LR
  U[👎 + comment] --> F[POST /api/feedback]
  F --> S[score user_feedback = false<br/>on the answer's trace]
  S --> T[03:00 triage job]
  T --> P{which layer failed?}
  P -->|retrieval · generation · tool routing · skipped search| DA[kubeflow/docs-agent]
  P -->|content gap| WG[component working group<br/>e.g. kubeflow/katib]
  T --> R[Markdown report<br/>+ triage scores]

docs.title: The feedback endpoint
docs.text:
POST /api/feedback on the public gateway (session token required, same rate limits as chat):

{"contextId": "<chat session id>", "turn": 0, "value": "down", "comment": "missing example YAML"}

The chat's contextId is its Langfuse session. Each user message is one trace in that session, so turn (0-based) picks the answer. The service writes a BOOLEAN score user_feedback with a fixed id, so changing a vote overwrites it. If the trace has not arrived yet, the vote is stored on the session instead.

Code: docs-agent-mcp/charts/gateway-guardrails/files/feedback.py (standard library only, run from a ConfigMap on a stock Python image).

docs.title: Triage
docs.text:
tests/feedback/triage.py feedback --since-hours 24 --write --report, run as a CronJob (triage.enabled in the docs-agent chart). For each thumbs-down:

  1. Read the question, tool calls, retrieved chunks and answer from the trace.
  2. Search the index again independently through the MCP server.
  3. Ask the judge whether the retrieved and the re-searched passages contain the answer, and whether the answer stayed grounded.
  4. Classify:
Layer Meaning Owner ok Retrieved the right content and answered from it – generation Retrieved the right content but answered badly docs-agent retrieval The index has the answer but the agent's search missed it docs-agent tool_routing A GitHub issue has the answer but the agent never searched issues docs-agent agent_skipped_retrieval The agent answered without searching docs-agent content_gap_handled The docs do not cover it and the agent said so component working group content_gap_hallucination The docs do not cover it and the agent answered anyway component working group (and docs-agent for the hallucination)

Results are stored as triage_layer and triage_component scores on the trace. The report in the Job log groups them by owner, with the user's comment. Nothing is filed automatically; a maintainer turns the report into issues.

Planned

Measuring the judge's agreement with human labels, and letting it choose the component from the question and the user's comment. Until then, treat the layer and component as suggestions for the person filing the issue.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Everything in the cluster is described in Git and deployed by Argo CD. This section is for maintainers and anyone running their own copy.

Page For Environments and delivery Production and staging in one cluster, and promoting a tested commit to production Argo CD The Applications and their sync policy, what lives where, deploys and rollbacks Observability Tracing to Langfuse, the live and evaluation projects, data retention Ingestion pipelines Loading docs, issues and code into Milvus with Kubeflow Pipelines

docs.title: Ground rules
docs.text:
• Git is the only writer. No kubectl edit on managed namespaces. A change is a pull request; Argo CD shows anything else as drift.
  • Secrets never go in Git. Charts reference Kubernetes Secrets by name. The list of Secrets to create is in deploy/argocd/README.md.
  • Production moves by promotion. It runs one commit of main, changed only by a promotion PR; reverting that PR rolls back.
  • GPU releases and Langfuse are synced by hand. llm-runtime and llm-judge restart a GPU pod and reload a model, and langfuse holds the trace data, so they never auto-sync.
  • CI never touches the cluster. It tests every PR and, on main, builds and pushes images. Argo CD deploys.

docs.title: Argo CD
docs.text: Argo CD deploys everything in the cluster from Git and shows any difference between Git and what is running.

docs.title: Applications
docs.text:
The root Application flo-apps (deploy/argocd/root.yaml) applies every Application in deploy/argocd/apps/ from main, so a new Application or a merged promotion takes effect without anyone running kubectl.

Application Source Tracks Namespace Sync flo-apps deploy/argocd/apps/ main argocd Automatic docs-agent docs-agent-mcp/charts/docs-agent + deploy/envs/prod/docs-agent.yaml promoted commit docs-agent Automatic gateway-guardrails docs-agent-mcp/charts/gateway-guardrails + deploy/envs/prod/ promoted commit docs-agent Automatic docs-agent-staging the docs-agent chart + deploy/envs/staging/docs-agent.yaml main docs-agent-staging Automatic, self-heal, prune otel-collector deploy/platform/otel-collector main docs-agent Automatic langfuse-retention deploy/platform/langfuse-retention main langfuse Automatic llm-runtime docs-agent-mcp/charts/llm-runtime main ml-infra Manual (GPU) llm-judge the same chart, Qwen profile main ml-infra Manual (GPU) langfuse Langfuse Helm chart + deploy/envs/prod/langfuse/values.yaml main langfuse Manual (stateful)

Chart Applications have two sources: the chart, and the values file from the same repository (referenced as $values). Both production sources are pinned to the promoted commit with a # prod-revision comment, which deploy/promote.sh moves. Image tags come from the synced commit ($ARGOCD_APP_REVISION_SHORT), not from values files.

llm-runtime and llm-judge stay manual because a sync restarts a GPU pod and reloads the model. langfuse stays manual because it holds the trace data; review its diff before syncing.

docs.title: What lives where
docs.text:
Kind of data Where Changed by Charts and Applications docs-agent-mcp/charts/, deploy/argocd/ Pull request Environment values (hosts, CORS origins) deploy/envs/<env>/ Pull request Production revision # prod-revision lines in deploy/argocd/apps/ Promotion PR (deploy/promote.sh) Secrets (API keys, Langfuse keys, passwords) Kubernetes Secrets, referenced by name Cluster admins

Values files are public, so nothing secret or personal goes in them.

docs.title: Day-to-day
docs.text:
• See what would change: open the Application, then App Diff, or run argocd app diff <app> --grpc-web with the read-only account.
  • Deploy production: open a promotion PR with deploy/promote.sh; merging it deploys.
  • Roll back: revert the promotion PR. Avoid History and Rollback in the UI: it pauses automatic sync and leaves Git and the cluster disagreeing.
  • Drift: a hand edit on an automatically synced Application is reverted (self-heal). On the manual ones it shows as OutOfSync until a sync or a change in Git resolves it.
  • GPU models and Langfuse: review the diff, then click Sync.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
The UI is behind the Istio gateway with HTTPS. There are two local accounts: admin for maintainers and viewer, which is read-only (it can see every Application, diff and log, but cannot sync or delete). Anonymous access and exec are disabled.

Install and account setup: deploy/argocd/README.md.

docs.title: Environments and delivery
docs.text:
One cluster runs two environments in separate namespaces. Staging runs every commit on main; production runs one commit that was promoted after its staging eval passed.

Production Staging Namespace docs-agent docs-agent-staging Argo CD application docs-agent, gateway-guardrails docs-agent-staging Tracks the commit in # prod-revision main Images <promoted commit> short SHA <latest commit> short SHA Sync automatic, when a promotion PR merges automatic, on every merge (self-heal, prune) Values deploy/envs/prod/ deploy/envs/staging/ Answer model llm (Gemma) the same llm Milvus collections kubeflow_docs, issues_rag, code_rag the same collections, read only Public Yes, through the gateway No; reached in-cluster through the kagent controller A2A API Langfuse live project, environment production evaluation project, environment staging After each sync nothing the eval Job

Staging shares the model and the vector database with production. Retrieval only reads, so staging uses the production collections; a change to ingestion that needs its own collection can point staging at one with mcp.config.docsCollection.

docs.title: Trunk-based delivery
docs.text: There are no long-lived environment branches. main is what staging runs, and production is a pointer to one commit of main. Production therefore gets exactly what staging tested: code, images, charts and values from the same commit. A release moves the pointer; a rollback moves it back.

docs.title: From merge to production
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  PR[PR merged to main] --> CI[CI builds both images<br/>tagged with the short SHA]
  PR --> S[Argo CD syncs staging<br/>to that commit and image]
  S --> E[Eval Job<br/>results in Langfuse]
  E --> P[Every week or two:<br/>deploy/promote.sh opens<br/>a promotion PR]
  P --> M[Promotion PR merged<br/>Argo CD syncs production]
  1. Build. Every push to main builds and pushes ghcr.io/kubeflow/mcp-kubeflow-docs:<short sha> and ghcr.io/kubeflow/kubeflow-session-issuer:<short sha>. CI never touches the cluster.
  2. Staging. The staging Application takes the image tag from the commit it syncs ($ARGOCD_APP_REVISION_SHORT), so every merge changes staging and triggers a sync. If Argo CD sees the commit before CI has pushed its image, the sync retries for up to 15 minutes.
  3. Eval. After the sync, the eval Job grades the deployed stack and records the run in Langfuse.

  4. Promote. Every week or two, a maintainer promotes the newest commit whose eval passed:

    deploy/promote.sh            # the tip of main
deploy/promote.sh 9145c31    # or a specific commit
deploy/promote.sh --open     # also push to your fork and open the PR

    The script checks that both images exist, moves every # prod-revision line in deploy/argocd/apps/ to the new commit, and writes the PR description: the commits since the current production and a table for that commit's staging eval scores, so each release keeps its scores in its PR.

  5. Production. Merging the promotion PR is the deploy: the root Application flo-apps applies the changed Applications, and docs-agent and gateway-guardrails sync to the new commit.

docs.title: Common changes
docs.text: Change Path MCP server code, charts, prompts, agent settings Merge → staging deploys and evaluates it → included in the next promotion Production-only setting (domain, CORS) PR to deploy/envs/prod/ → takes effect with the next promotion Answer or judge model PR to the llm-runtime values → manual sync (GPU restart) Rollback Revert the promotion PR; Argo CD syncs production back to the previous commit Hand edit in the cluster Argo CD reverts it (self-heal) on every automatically synced Application

docs.title: Kubeflow RAG pipelines
docs.text: Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) definitions for indexing Kubeflow documentation and related corpora into Milvus.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Path Role kubeflow-pipeline.py Production docs v4 pipeline: GitHub docs download → chunk/embed → Milvus store issues-pipeline.py GitHub issues RAG pipeline code-pipeline.py GitHub code/manifests RAG pipeline utils/ Shared helpers used by the live pipelines: ingest, parsers, Milvus store, TEI Dockerfile.pipeline Slim ingest image (docs-rag-ingest) that copies docs helpers from utils/ as flat /app modules github_rag_pipeline.yaml Compiled docs pipeline (regenerate via python kubeflow-pipeline.py) legacy/pipelines/ (repo root) Older pipelines, including incremental docs ingest — not the live v4 docs path

docs.title: Docs pipeline (core)
docs.text:
Purpose: Full rebuild of the documentation corpus into the v4 hybrid Milvus collection (kubeflow_docs).

  1. Download GitHub directory — .md / .html under a repo path (stock Python image)
  2. Chunk and embed — thin step that imports hugo_ingest / canonical_rag_ingest from the ingest image, then POSTs to TEI
  3. Store in Milvus — thin step that imports milvus_store helpers from the same image

Compile writes the YAML recipe (no Docker required). A cluster run needs the ingest image:

cd docs-agent-mcp/pipelines
# Optional: pin a built tag (default is ghcr.io/kubeflow/docs-rag-ingest:v0.1.0)
# set DOCS_INGEST_IMAGE=ghcr.io/kubeflow/docs-rag-ingest:<tag>
python kubeflow-pipeline.py

Key defaults: target_tokens=350, overlap_tokens=50, 768-d dense vectors, explicit clean_rebuild confirmation for destructive drops.

docs.title: Issues and code pipelines
docs.text:
Compile from the pipelines directory (same as CI):

python issues-pipeline.py
python code-pipeline.py

These pipelines are self-contained KFP components. Parsers and test helpers live in utils/issues_utils.py and utils/code_utils.py.

docs.title: Incremental docs ingest
docs.text: The incremental GitHub docs pipeline lives under legacy/pipelines/incremental-pipeline.py. It predates v4 hybrid schema and is kept for reference only; use kubeflow-pipeline.py for production docs indexing.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
See requirements.txt. Compile-time needs kfp (and optionally kfp-kubernetes for secret wiring in cluster runs).

This page is docs-agent-mcp/pipelines/README.md from the repository, included as is so there is one copy. Edit it there.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text: Every chat produces a trace in Langfuse: the agent run, each model call, each tool call, the retrieval and the query embedding. Traces from production and staging go to different Langfuse projects, so evaluation runs never mix with real user conversations.

docs.title: Where spans come from
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph prod[docs-agent]
    A1[agents] --> OT
    M1[MCP server]
  end
  subgraph stg[docs-agent-staging]
    A2[agents] --> OT
    M2[MCP server]
    EJ[eval Job]
  end
  OT[OTel collector<br/>k8sattributes + routing] -->|namespace docs-agent<br/>environment=production| LIVE[(Langfuse live project)]
  OT -->|namespace docs-agent-staging<br/>environment=staging| EVAL[(Langfuse evaluation project)]
  M1 -->|Langfuse SDK, live keys| LIVE
  M2 -->|Langfuse SDK, eval keys| EVAL
  EJ -->|experiment spans + scores| EVAL
Source How What you see kagent agents OpenTelemetry, endpoint set by the kagent controller AGENT and GENERATION observations: prompts, tool calls, answers, tokens, latency MCP server Langfuse SDK (flo_tracing.py), off unless keys are set TOOL, RETRIEVER (hit count, mode, intent, top scores) and EMBEDDING observations Eval Job OTLP experiment spans and the Scores API Experiments on the flo-e2e dataset with routing and groundedness scores Feedback service Scores API user_feedback on the answer's trace Triage job Scores API triage_layer, triage_component

docs.title: The collector
docs.text:
The agents' tracing endpoint is set by the shared kagent controller, so agents in both namespaces send to the same collector. kagent's runtime does not apply OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, so agents cannot label their own environment. Instead, the collector's k8sattributes processor looks up the namespace of the pod that sent each span and a routing connector picks the project:

  • docs-agent-staging → evaluation project, langfuse.environment=staging
  • everything else → live project, langfuse.environment=production

It also drops framework transport spans (a2a.server.*, bare HTTP spans) that would bury the agent, tool and model spans. Config: deploy/platform/otel-collector/.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
Project Contents Who Live Real user questions, feedback, triage Maintainers and mentors only Evaluation Eval runs from staging, per commit and PR Maintainers, plus a shared read-only community account

The projects are in separate Langfuse organizations, because per-project roles need Langfuse Enterprise; organization-level Viewer works in the open-source edition.

docs.title: Data retention
docs.text:
Self-hosted Langfuse keeps data forever unless you use its Enterprise retention feature, so a weekly CronJob (deploy/platform/langfuse-retention, Sundays 04:00 UTC) deletes old data per project:

Project Kept for Deleted Live 4 weeks traces, observations, scores (including user_feedback) and raw events, in ClickHouse and in the S3 store Evaluation 2 weeks the same; each release's scores stay in its promotion PR

Datasets, including the eval questions, are never deleted. The windows are in the job's ConfigMap; setting DRY_RUN to "true" only prints what would be deleted.

docs.title: Reading a trace
docs.text:
1. Open the project and go to Traces (or Sessions: the session id is the chat's A2A contextId).
  2. Filter by Environment, by session, or by a score such as user_feedback = false.
  3. Open a trace: the tree shows the agent run, then each model call and tool call. Retriever observations show which search mode the intent router chose and how many hits came back.
